name: Paekche
confidence_why: One first-hand description, read in part (the publisher's preview); the passage read states the pattern recorded here and was checked; 11 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

The mirror copy of A's abstract file was absent (mirror not yet filled); I re-saved the abstract from the KCI page to Reading 'unclear or contradictory' + statement_type 'tone' is the right encoding of a hedged 'no tones' inference from toponym phonograms with nothing on stres…
new_statements.relation_note: Abstract: consonantal codas not phonemic in Paekche; nucleus system unrecoverable; 'tones do not seem to have been in the Paekche language'. Full text (Korean) behind Kyobo Scholar login; KCI's own preview endpoint returned a blank watermark page.
new_statements.rule_in_words: From the phonographic spellings of Paekche place names the author infers that Paekche had no phonemic stop/nasal codas and, further, no lexical tones; nothing is said about stress/accent placement. A hedged negative tone statement for an extinct, fragmentarily attested language; no word-prosodic type can be assigned.
new_statements.exceptions: none in the abstract; the evidential basis (how tonelessness is inferred from sinographic transcription) is in the unread body
new_statements.identity_note: Sino-Paekche = readings of Chinese characters used as phonograms in Paekche toponyms of the Samguk sagi (the core Paekche corpus itself); the author draws his conclusion for 'the Paekche language' (1st c. BC - 7th c. AD, SW Korean peninsula). Same languoid as paek1234; not Silla/Old Korean proper, which he contrasts (Unified Silla after the 8th c.).

new_statements.quote: 이와사키본에 보이는 「上·去⇔a」의 대응관계에 대하여 권인한(2005)은 고대 한국어의 성조가 한어 중고음과는 상당히 다른 체계임을 암시한다고 논하며, 고대한국어의 성조가 반영되었고 한어 중고음과는 다른 체계라고 주장한다. 마에다본의 한국고유명의 성점이 고대한국어의 성조를 반영하였는지에 대해서는 다각도의 검토가 필요하지만 적어도 한국고유명의 성조체계는 a점, 즉 ‘평성화’임을 전망할 수 있다.
new_statements.translation: On the correspondence 'MC rising/departing <-> a [low level dot]' seen in the Iwasaki-bon, Kwon In-han (2005) argues that it implies that the tone of Old Korean was a system quite different from Middle Chinese, i.e. that Old Korean tone is reflected and that it differs from MC. Whether the tone dots on the Korean proper names of the Maeda-bon reflect Old Korean tone needs examination from several angles, but at least one can foresee that the tonal system of the Korean proper names is the a-dot, i.e. 'level-tone-ization'.
new_statements.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2014. 前田本『日本書紀』한국 고유명의 声点에 대하여 [Tone marks of the proper nouns of Korean origin in the Maeda manuscript of Nihonsyoki]. 日語日文學 (대한일어일문학회) 62: 67-81. doi:10.18631/jalali.2014.62.004. KCI ART001878184.
new_statements.locator: §4.1, journal p.76 (p.10); data tables <표1>-<표3> pp.69-72; conclusion §6 p.79 (p.13): '마에다본 일본서기 한국고유명의 성조는 ‘평성’으로 가점되는 양상을 보이며, 이는 이와사키본의 결과와 같다'
new_statements.relation_note: Presents all tone-dotted Korean proper names of the Maeda-bon (377 dots vs 321 on Japanese names), correlates them with MC tone, Middle Sino-Korean tone (平⇔L, 上去⇔R~H, 入⇔H) and Go-on/Kan-on: Korean names show 平·上·去⇔a, 入⇔d ('평성화', the 'low tone phenomenon' of the English abstract), the same as Kwon found in the Iwasaki-bon although the two manuscripts share no volume; hence a common transmitted system for intoning Korean names. Reports Kwon's view that Old Korean tone (different from MC) is reflected; leaves that open.
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Maeda manuscript the characters spelling Korean (largely Paekche) names carry tone dots that collapse Middle-Chinese level, rising and departing tones onto the low-level dot (a) and keep entering tone as d; the marking agrees neither with MC, Middle Sino-Korean, Go-on nor Kan-on. Kwon 2005 takes this as a reflex of an Old Korean tonal system unlike Chinese; Park only concludes a 'level-tone marking' convention for Korean names shared across manuscript lineages. No word-prosodic type for Paekche follows.
new_statements.exceptions: characters with variant dots across attestations (∼) listed per item; a few b/c (high/rising) dots on 濟, 政, 至 etc. (표6)
new_statements.identity_note: Object = tone dots (声点) written on the Chinese characters of 'Korean-origin proper names' (persons, places, ranks, book titles) in the 11th-12th c. Maeda-bon of Nihon shoki vols 11, 14, 17, 20; the tables label each item and the plurality are 百済人/百済地名/百済官位/百済書名 (c. 48 items) beside 新羅 (28), 加羅 (28), 高句麗 (5), 任那, 耽羅; the analysis pools them as '한국 고유명'. Evidence is Japanese glossators' reading tradition of an 8th-c. text, several centuries after Paekche, not Paekche speech. | Same object in the 12th-c. Zushoryō-bon (vols 2, 10, 12-17, 21-24): Korean-origin proper names of Nihon shoki, Paekche items pooled with Silla/Kara/Koguryŏ ones. | 16th-c. Urabe Kanemigi-bon covering all 30 volumes, hence the fullest set of dotted Korean-origin (Paekche, Silla, Kara, Koguryŏ) names; pooled analysis. | Tone dots on the katakana glosses (傍訓) of Korean names in Maeda/Zushoryō/Kanemigi manuscripts; the examples named in the abstract — コキシ (kokishi 'king' as in 百済王), ニリム (nirimu 主 'lord'), サシ (sashi 城 'fort'), ツクソクロ — are precisely the Paekche glosses of Nihon shoki that make up the paek1234 corpus (Bentley 2000, Kōno 1987), though the paper speaks of '古代韓国語'. | A dialect-accent project (S. Korean coast vs N. Kyushu) whose historical narrative names 百済語 alongside 高句麗語/新羅語; no Paekche data are used — the Three-Kingdoms statements are inferences from modern accent geography.

new_statements.quote: 특히 「上·去⇔a」의 대응에 대하여 権仁瀚(2005)는 고대 한국어의 성조가 한어 중고음과는 상당히 다른 체계임을 암시한다고 논하며, 고대 한국어의 성조가 반영되었고 중고한어음과는 다른 체계라고 주장한다. 박미현(2014)에서 마에다본에 대해 논하였듯이 도쇼료본 또한 한국고유명의 성점이 고대 한국어의 성조를 반영하였는지에 대해서는 다각도의 검토가 필요하지만 한국고유명의 성조체계는 a점, 즉 평성으로 가점되는 경향이 있다고 할 수 있다. 본고에서는 이를 ‘평성 가점화’라고 칭하겠다.
new_statements.translation: In particular, on the correspondence 'rising/departing <-> a', Kwon In-han (2005) argues that it implies Old Korean tone was a system quite different from MC, that Old Korean tone is reflected and differs from MC. As argued for the Maeda-bon in Park (2014), whether the Zushoryō-bon tone dots on Korean proper names reflect Old Korean tone needs multi-angle examination, but the tonal system of Korean proper names tends to be dotted a, i.e. level tone; I call this 'level-tone dotting'.
new_statements.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2015. 圖書寮本『日本書紀』에 보이는 한국계 고유명의 声点 연구 [Tone marks of the proper nouns of Korean origin in the Toshoryo manuscript of Nihonsyoki]. 日語日文學 66: 57-72. doi:10.18631/jalali.2015.66.004. KCI ART001993153.
new_statements.locator: §3, journal p.60 (p.4); §4 pp.60-61 adds that 高山倫明 1981 and 尹幸舜 1995 show Japanese (Heian accent / Suiko-period Go-on) interference cannot be excluded
new_statements.relation_note: Extends the tone-dot corpus to the Zushoryō-bon; same 'level-tone dotting' of Korean (incl. Paekche) names, not parallel to MC or to Go-on/Kan-on; explicitly notes (via Takayama 1981, Yun 1995) that Nihon shoki manuscript dots reflect Heian-period Japanese accent / Tang northern readings, so Japanese interference on the Korean names cannot be ruled out.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zushoryō-bon repeats the Iwasaki/Maeda pattern: MC 平上去 -> a (low level), 入 -> d on Korean names; author names it '평성 가점화' and treats the names as usable Old-Korean data while flagging possible Japanese interference. No Paekche-specific prosodic rule.
new_statements.exceptions: items with Japanese interference; variant dots across copies

new_statements.quote: 즉, 중국 중고음의 상성과 거성은 가네미기본에서 평성으로, 일본 오음의 거성은 평성으로, 일본 한음의 상성과 거성은 평성으로 가점되는 ‘평성화’가 보인다. 이로서 한국계 고유명사는 중국 중고음과 평행하지 않으며, 일본 오음과 일본 한음의 영향을 일방적으로 받지 않았음으로 알 수 있다.
new_statements.translation: That is, MC rising and departing tones are dotted as level tone in the Kanemigi-bon, Go-on departing as level, Kan-on rising and departing as level: a 'level-tone-ization'. Hence the Korean-origin proper names do not run parallel to Middle Chinese and were not one-sidedly influenced by Go-on or Kan-on.
new_statements.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2016. 兼右本『일본서기』에 보이는 한국계 고유명사의 성점(聲點) 연구 [A study on the tone marks for proper nouns of Korean origin in the Kanemigi-bon of Nihonsyoki]. 일본어문학 (일본어문학회, Daegu) 74: 21-42. doi:10.21792/trijpn.2016.74.002. KCI ART002135402.
new_statements.locator: Ⅴ. 결론, journal p.34 (p.14); Japanese abstract p.21 ('この「平声加点傾向」は…韓国系固有名詞の声点の特徴であると言える')
new_statements.relation_note: Largest data set of the series; '平声加点傾向' confirmed for single and multiple dots; introduction (p.22) summarizes Kwon 2005 as showing the Iwasaki-bon Korean names 'do not simply reflect MC or Go-on/Kan-on and can be used as Korean-language material' and Park 2014/2015 as showing the same for Maeda/Zushoryō.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Across red circle dots, red line dots and black dots of the Kanemigi-bon, Korean-origin names again show the level-tone dotting (上/去 -> 平) independent of MC and of both Japanese Sino-reading strata; the manuscript is judged usable 'as Korean-language data' to make up for the small old-manuscript corpus. Nothing on stress; no Paekche-specific system.
new_statements.exceptions: uneven distribution of the three dot types by volume (faithful copying of different exemplars)

new_statements.quote: また、傍訓の声点は固定型と非固定型に二分される。固定型はコキシ、ツクソクロのように低平調に固定されて伝写されたもので、非固定型はサシ、ニリムのように固定されず伝写されてきたものであると言える。非固定型は古代韓国語の多様な声調を反映すると言える。
new_statements.translation: The tone dots on the side-glosses divide into a fixed type and a non-fixed type. The fixed type, like kokishi and tsukusokuro, was transmitted fixed on a low level tone; the non-fixed type, like sashi and nirimu, was transmitted without being fixed. The non-fixed type can be said to reflect the diverse tones of Old Korean.
new_statements.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2021. 『일본서기』 고사본의 한국 고유명에 가점된 방훈(傍訓)의 성점 연구 [A study of the tone marks on the katakana side-glosses of Korean proper names in old manuscripts of Nihon shoki]. 일본어문학 (일본어문학회) 94.
new_statements.locator: author's Japanese and English abstracts (RISS record); body pp. not seen (Kyobo Scholar login)
new_statements.relation_note: Abstract: side-gloss dots occur mainly on place names; fixed type = low-level throughout (コキシ, ツクソクロ), non-fixed type (サシ, ニリム) 'reflects the diverse tones of Old Korean'; quantity small; caution needed because of Japanese interference. Full text behind Kyobo Scholar; companion Park 2022 (日本語文學 99: 67-88, login) treats only the graphic form (圏点 vs 線点) of the dots on Korean names.
new_statements.rule_in_words: For kana-glossed Paekche words in Nihon shoki manuscripts the glossators' pitch dots are either frozen low-level (kokishi 'king', tsukusokuro) or variable across copies (sashi 'fort', nirimu 'lord'); the author proposes that the variable ones preserve 'various tones of Old Korean', while warning of Japanese interference. This is the only claim anywhere that a prosodic property of actual Paekche lexemes is recoverable; it assigns no system (no H/L pattern per word is given in the abstract) and rests on 11th-16th c. Japanese reading marks.
new_statements.exceptions: 'some of these accent marks were interfered with by Japanese' (abstract)

new_statements.quote: その後、三国時代にはいり、その後期になり、半島の北半分を支配する高句麗は依然としてアクセントを持たず、半島南東部は百済、新羅が台頭し、中世語型アクセントと慶尚道方言型アクセントの分岐が開始した可能性が高く、少なくともそのような変化を起こすきっかけが作動したと考える。
new_statements.translation: Then, in the Three Kingdoms period, in its later part, Koguryŏ ruling the northern half of the peninsula still had no accent, while in the south(-east) Paekche and Silla rose and the split between the Middle-Korean-type accent and the Kyŏngsang-dialect-type accent very probably began, or at least the trigger for such a change was set off.
new_statements.citation: 板橋義三 (Itabashi, Yoshizo). 2019. 科学研究費助成事業 研究成果報告書, 基盤研究(C) 26370488「韓国南部方言と九州北部方言のアクセント型の同源性の有無に関する通時的・実証的研究」[A Historical/Theoretical Study on the Genealogy of the Pitch Accent Patterns of Kyushu Dialects and of the Southern Coastal Dialects of Korean], Kyushu University, FY2014-2018. 5 pp.
new_statements.locator: ４．研究成果, p.4 (of 5); English outline p.1: 'Proto-Japanese is most likely to have had pitch accent, whereas Old Korean did not have any type of accent system'; keywords include 古代朝鮮語と朝鮮祖語のアクセントの非存在
new_statements.relation_note: States that Old Korean and Proto-Korean/Proto-Puyŏ lacked accent, that a pre-Japanese substratum sat under Koguryŏ, Paekche and Silla without affecting accent, and that MK-type vs Kyŏngsang-type accent began to diverge when Paekche and Silla rose. Book-length version: Itabashi 2019, 日本語と朝鮮語の方言アクセント体系と両言語の歴史的関係に関する理論的・実証的研究, 現代図書, ISBN 9784434258244 (print). Related print items from the same circle: 金瑜晶 (Kim Yujeong) 2016, 2018 '古代朝鮮語のアクセントの再構', 日韓比較言語文化研究 4: 133-136; 5: 69-89 (NDL bib 028064125, 029498828).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Author's scenario: Proto-Korean/Proto-Puyŏ and early Old Korean were accentless ('non-distinctive accent'); pitch accent arose late in the Three Kingdoms period in the Paekche/Silla south and spread with Silla; Koguryŏ stayed accentless. A speculative reconstruction narrative, internally awkward for Paekche (accentless Old Korean vs accent genesis in the Paekche-Silla zone), with no Paekche evidence; not a descriptive statement.

Korean coast vs N. Kyushu) whose historical narrative names 百済語 alongside 高句麗語/新羅語; no Paekche data are used — the Three-Kingdoms statements are inferences from modern accent geography.

Also: Park 2017, 『釋日本紀』 한국계 고유명의 성점 [Tone marks of the proper nouns of Korean origin in the Shaku Nihongi], 日本硏究 44, doi:10.20404/jscau.2017.02.44.43 (record only).
tone_statements.quote: 즉 중국 중고음 평성, 상성, 거성은 석일본기에서 A점(평성)으로 가점 되었고 이는 중고음의 고평조와 상승조가 석일본기에서는 저평조로 발화되었음을 의미한다. 이와 같은 한국계 고유명사 성점의 평성화에 대해서는 권인한(2005), 박미현(2014,2015,2016)의 결과와 같다. 권인한(2005)은 고사본 중 가장 오래된 이와사키본(岩崎本)을, 박미현(2014,2015,2016)은 이와사키본과는 계통을 달리하는 마에다본(前田本)과 도쇼료본(圖書寮), 우라베케 계통인 가네미기본(兼右本)을 조사하여 중고음의 상성과 거성이 고사본에서는 평성으로 가점되었음을 논하고 한국어 연구 자료로 이용 가능함9)을 제시하였다.
tone_statements.translation: That is, Middle Chinese level, rising and departing tones were marked with the A dot (level tone) in the Shaku Nihongi, which means that the high-level and rising contours of Middle Chinese were pronounced as low-level in the Shaku Nihongi. This 'level-tone shift' of the tone marks on Korean-origin proper nouns agrees with the results of Kwon In-han (2005) and Park Mi-Hyun (2014, 2015, 2016). Kwon (2005) examined the oldest manuscript, the Iwasaki-bon, and Park (2014, 2015, 2016) the Maeda-bon and Toshoryo-bon, of a different lineage from the Iwasaki-bon, and the Kanemigi-bon of the Urabe lineage, arguing that Middle Chinese rising and departing tones were marked as level tone in the old manuscripts and proposing that [these marks] can be used as material for the study of Korean.
tone_statements.locator: p. 48, section 3 '중국 중고음 성조와의 대응관계' (section runs pp. 47-48; section 4 begins on p. 49)

tone_statements.citation: Eom, Ik-sang (엄익상). 2007. 백제한자음의 운모와 성조에 대한 의문 [Some Questions on the Final and Tonal Systems of Sino-Paekche Korean]. 중국언어연구 (Korea Journal of Chinese Linguistics, 한국중국언어학회) 25: 47-66. ISSN 1229-554X. KCI ART001227750.
tone_statements.quote: Through careful examination on the characters with consonantal codas, this article concludes that both stop and nasal endings were not phonemic in Paekche while they seem to be in the process of becoming phonemes in the Unified Silla after the eighth century. … The data given in the Samguk sagi, however, do not give enough information to draw the nucleus system of Sino-Paekche. Furthermore, tones do not seem to have been in the Paekche language.

sources.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2021. 『일본서기』 고사본의 한국 고유명에 가점된 방훈(傍訓)의 성점 연구 [A study of the tone marks on the katakana side-glosses of Korean proper names in old manuscripts of Nihon shoki]. 일본어문학 (일본어문학회) 94.
sources.access_detail: digital copy exists; only the abstract or an excerpt is open
sources.quote: また、傍訓の声点は固定型と非固定型に二分される。固定型はコキシ、ツクソクロのように低平調に固定されて伝写されたもので、非固定型はサシ、ニリムのように固定されず伝写されてきたものであると言える。非固定型は古代韓国語の多様な声調を反映すると言える。
sources.locator: author's Japanese and English abstracts (RISS record); body pp. not seen (Kyobo Scholar login)
sources.note: Abstract: side-gloss dots occur mainly on place names; fixed type = low-level throughout (コキシ, ツクソクロ), non-fixed type (サシ, ニリム) 'reflects the diverse tones of Old Korean'; quantity small; caution needed because of Japanese interference. Full text behind Kyobo Scholar; companion Park 2022 (日本語文學 99: 67-88, login) treats only the graphic form (圏点 vs 線点) of the dots on Korean names.

sources.citation: 板橋義三 (Itabashi, Yoshizo). 2019. 科学研究費助成事業 研究成果報告書, 基盤研究(C) 26370488「韓国南部方言と九州北部方言のアクセント型の同源性の有無に関する通時的・実証的研究」[A Historical/Theoretical Study on the Genealogy of the Pitch Accent Patterns of Kyushu Dialects and of the Southern Coastal Dialects of Korean], Kyushu University, FY2014-2018. 5 pp.
sources.quote: その後、三国時代にはいり、その後期になり、半島の北半分を支配する高句麗は依然としてアクセントを持たず、半島南東部は百済、新羅が台頭し、中世語型アクセントと慶尚道方言型アクセントの分岐が開始した可能性が高く、少なくともそのような変化を起こすきっかけが作動したと考える。
sources.locator: ４．研究成果, p.4 (of 5); English outline p.1: 'Proto-Japanese is most likely to have had pitch accent, whereas Old Korean did not have any type of accent system'; keywords include 古代朝鮮語と朝鮮祖語のアクセントの非存在
sources.note: States that Old Korean and Proto-Korean/Proto-Puyŏ lacked accent, that a pre-Japanese substratum sat under Koguryŏ, Paekche and Silla without affecting accent, and that MK-type vs Kyŏngsang-type accent began to diverge when Paekche and Silla rose. Book-length version: Itabashi 2019, 日本語と朝鮮語の方言アクセント体系と両言語の歴史的関係に関する理論的・実証的研究, 現代図書, ISBN 9784434258244 (print). Related print items from the same circle: 金瑜晶 (Kim Yujeong) 2016, 2018 '古代朝鮮語のアクセントの再構', 日韓比較言語文化研究 4: 133-136; 5: 69-89 (NDL bib 028064125, 029498828).

sources.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2016. 兼右本『일본서기』에 보이는 한국계 고유명사의 성점(聲點) 연구 [A study on the tone marks for proper nouns of Korean origin in the Kanemigi-bon of Nihonsyoki]. 일본어문학 (일본어문학회, Daegu) 74: 21-42. doi:10.21792/trijpn.2016.74.002. KCI ART002135402.
sources.quote: 즉, 중국 중고음의 상성과 거성은 가네미기본에서 평성으로, 일본 오음의 거성은 평성으로, 일본 한음의 상성과 거성은 평성으로 가점되는 ‘평성화’가 보인다. 이로서 한국계 고유명사는 중국 중고음과 평행하지 않으며, 일본 오음과 일본 한음의 영향을 일방적으로 받지 않았음으로 알 수 있다.
sources.locator: Ⅴ. 결론, journal p.34 (p.14); Japanese abstract p.21 ('この「平声加点傾向」は…韓国系固有名詞の声点の特徴であると言える')
sources.note: Largest data set of the series; '平声加点傾向' confirmed for single and multiple dots; introduction (p.22) summarizes Kwon 2005 as showing the Iwasaki-bon Korean names 'do not simply reflect MC or Go-on/Kan-on and can be used as Korean-language material' and Park 2014/2015 as showing the same for Maeda/Zushoryō.

sources.citation: Park, Mi-Hyun (박미현). 2015. 圖書寮本『日本書紀』에 보이는 한국계 고유명의 声点 연구 [Tone marks of the proper nouns of Korean origin in the Toshoryo manuscript of Nihonsyoki]. 日語日文學 66: 57-72. doi:10.18631/jalali.2015.66.004. KCI ART001993153.
sources.quote: 특히 「上·去⇔a」의 대응에 대하여 権仁瀚(2005)는 고대 한국어의 성조가 한어 중고음과는 상당히 다른 체계임을 암시한다고 논하며, 고대 한국어의 성조가 반영되었고 중고한어음과는 다른 체계라고 주장한다. 박미현(2014)에서 마에다본에 대해 논하였듯이 도쇼료본 또한 한국고유명의 성점이 고대 한국어의 성조를 반영하였는지에 대해서는 다각도의 검토가 필요하지만 한국고유명의 성조체계는 a점, 즉 평성으로 가점되는 경향이 있다고 할 수 있다. 본고에서는 이를 ‘평성 가점화’라고 칭하겠다.
sources.locator: §3, journal p.60 (p.4); §4 pp.60-61 adds that 高山倫明 1981 and 尹幸舜 1995 show Japanese (Heian accent / Suiko-period Go-on) interference cannot be excluded
sources.note: Extends the tone-dot corpus to the Zushoryō-bon; same 'level-tone dotting' of Korean (incl. Paekche) names, not parallel to MC or to Go-on/Kan-on; explicitly notes (via Takayama 1981, Yun 1995) that Nihon shoki manuscript dots reflect Heian-period Japanese accent / Tang northern readings, so Japanese interference on the Korean names cannot be ruled out.

sources.locator: §4.1, journal p.76 (p.10); data tables <표1>-<표3> pp.69-72; conclusion §6 p.79 (p.13): '마에다본 일본서기 한국고유명의 성조는 ‘평성’으로 가점되는 양상을 보이며, 이는 이와사키본의 결과와 같다'
sources.note: Presents all tone-dotted Korean proper names of the Maeda-bon (377 dots vs 321 on Japanese names), correlates them with MC tone, Middle Sino-Korean tone (平⇔L, 上去⇔R~H, 入⇔H) and Go-on/Kan-on: Korean names show 平·上·去⇔a, 入⇔d ('평성화', the 'low tone phenomenon' of the English abstract), the same as Kwon found in the Iwasaki-bon although the two manuscripts share no volume; hence a common transmitted system for intoning Korean names. Reports Kwon's view that Old Korean tone (different from MC) is reflected; leaves that open.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Baekje language' (accessed 2026-09-17), summarizing Vovin 2005/2013, Bentley 2000, Kōno 1987, Lee & Ramsey 2011, Lee Seungjae 2017.
sources.note: No phonology; states the corpus (42 Nihon shoki words, 3 Zhou shu, 4 Liang shu, mokkan names with 147 phonographic characters, unglossed Samguk sagi toponyms) 'is insufficient to allow a reconstruction of the phonology'.

sources.citation: 遠藤光暁 (Endō Mitsuaki). 2023. 於羅瑕と鞬吉支 [Orake and Konkishi: the oldest Sino-Japanese/Korean readings of words for 'king', 'country', 'capital']. 青山經濟論集 (Aoyama Keizai Ronshū) 74(4): 33-56. CiNii crid 1390577851239863168.
sources.note: No prosodic content for Paekche: discusses segmental shape of 於羅 (first syllable vowel, *hVCV stems, aspiration from vowel loss), 瑕 = 加/干 'chief', 鞬 + 吉支; the only tone word in the paper (去声 -s of 帯 in Baxter-Sagart OC) concerns a Japanese name spelling (p.51-52), not Paekche. Silent on stress/accent/tone of Paekche.

sources.citation: Lee, SeungJae (李丞宰 / イ・スンジェ, Seoul National University); Japanese translation 2020. 古代漢字音の音韻対立研究方法論 — 高句麗語、百濟語、中国前期中古漢語を中心に [Methodology for studying phonological oppositions in ancient Sino-readings: Koguryŏ, Paekche and Early Middle Chinese]. 韓国語学年報 (Annual Journal of Korean Linguistics, Kanda University of International Studies) 16: 139-191.
sources.note: Image-only PDF (text = page numbers); Japanese scanned of 30 of 53 pages. Content: Prague-school minimal-pair method applied to Sino-readings; 声調 (tone) figures only as one of the five components of a Chinese syllable [聲母, 開合, 等呼, 聲調, 韻] used to define 同韻 minimal pairs; results are consonant inventories (Paekche has a full voiced/voiceless opposition and marginal aspirates; velar-glottal merger). No claim about Paekche tone, accent or stress in the pages read.

sources.note: Data/transmission study, no claim about Paekche (or Old Korean) prosody of its own. Findings: of 741 dots on Korean-origin names 509 (68%) are 平聲 (74 上, 64 去, 94 入); 95% agreement with the Kanemigi-bon; p.54-55 reports that Kwon 2005 (Iwasaki-bon) and Park 2014/2015/2016 found the same 平聲 dotting tendency and argued it does not mirror Middle Chinese tone ('고평조인 상성과 상승조인 거성을 저평조인 평성으로 가점했기 때문'), and that Japanese proper names in the Maeda-bon are by contrast dotted 上聲. p.52 gives the dot values used (平 L, 上 H, 去 R, 入 L) with the example 蓋鹵王 = 入-上-上 'LHH'.

sources.citation: Lee, Janghee (이장희). 2014. 고대국어의 음운체계 연구의 새로운 시각 - 이승재, 『漢字音으로 본 백제어 자음체계』(태학사, 2013) - [A new vision of ancient Korean phonological research: review of Lee SeungJae 2013]. 어문론총 (Korean Language and Literature) 62: 585-593. doi:10.22784/eomun.2014.62.585. KCI ART001943085 (open PDF).
sources.note: Confirms that Lee SeungJae's 2013 monograph (7 chapters + appendix of Paekche phonogram values) deals with data collation, orthography and the consonant system only (voiced series, affricates, codas); tone is not a topic. Useful to close off the 2013 book as a prosody source without library access.

sources.citation: Kim, Jung-vin (金正彬 / 김정빈). 2007. 『日本書紀』에 보이는 백제 한자음 연구 ―그 자료성과 음운체계를 중심으로― [A study of ancient Baekje Chinese-readings from Ilbonseogi (Nihon shoki): their value as data and the phonological system]. 구결연구 (Kugyol Studies) 19: 25-62. doi:10.17001/kugyol.2007.19.002. KCI ART001078160 (open PDF KCI_FI001078160).
sources.note: Treats initials (聲母) and finals (韻母) of the Nihon shoki Paekche phonograms against the α/β strata of Old Japanese transcription and Middle Chinese; concludes the compilers' 8th-c. phonological awareness contaminates the data and that the usable system 'does not differ greatly from modern Korean'. Silent on Paekche tone/accent/stress.

sources.citation: Bentley, John R. 2000. A New Look at Paekche and Korean: Data from Nihon shoki. Language Research (어학연구, Seoul National University) 36(2): 417-443.
sources.note: Nothing on Paekche stress/accent. Segmental reconstruction of ~40 Paekche words from Nihon shoki phonograms; p.423: 'I have also ignored Starostin's distinction of long vowels, tones, and aspiration because I do not think these correspond to anything in Paekche.' Middle Korean tone (R, LH) is cited only for MK cognates.

sources.citation: 板橋義三 (Itabashi Yoshizo). 1996. 高句麗、新羅、百済の古代三国における『尸』の音価とその言語的相違 [The linguistic discrepancies among the Three Kingdoms in the Old Korean period seen by examining the phonological value of the character 尸]. 言語科学 (Kyushu University) 31: 15-38. doi:10.15017/6796331.
sources.note: Segmental: the sound value of the phonogram 尸 (-l/-r vs -s) across the three kingdoms as evidence that their languages differed. Nothing prosodic.

sources.citation: Kortlandt, Frederik. 1993. The origin of the Japanese and Korean accent systems. Acta Linguistica Hafniensia 26: 57-65 (web edition 2003, art125e; reprinted in Transeurasian Linguistics vol. II: Phonology, London: Routledge 2017, 269-276; also in Selected Writings on Slavic and General Linguistics, 2011).
sources.note: States explicitly that the tone patterns of Paekche are unknown; the four MK/OJ loanword pairs with mismatched pitch patterns (Buddha, temple, district, hatchet) are the only Paekche-related prosodic data point, and they are left unexplained. Useful as an authority for 'no prosodic information recoverable'.

sources.citation: Kōno, Rokurō. 1987. The Bilingualism of the Paekche Language. Memoirs of the Research Department of the Toyo Bunko 45: 75-86.
sources.note: Nothing on Paekche stress/accent. Uses Middle Korean rising-tone marks (two dots) as evidence that MK monosyllables (nim, nui, moi) contract earlier disyllabic *X-ri (low-high) forms seen in Nihon shoki Paekche glosses (nirimu, mure); no claim about Paekche prosody itself.

sources.citation: 馬淵和夫・洪思満・李寅泳・大橋康子 (Mabuchi Kazuo et al., 古代朝鮮語研究会). 1979. 『三国史記』記載の百済地名より見た古代百済語の考察 [On the Ancient Language of Kudara as Reflected in Kudara Place Names in the Sangokushiki]. 文藝言語研究 言語篇 (University of Tsukuba) 3: 73-127.
sources.note: Chapter 3 reconstructs the Paekche sound system from toponym phonograms read in Old Chinese values (Tung T'ung-ho): word-initial consonants (k, t, p, s, ts?, m, n, j..), apparently no voicing contrast, medial consonants, a five-vowel system /a i u o ə/, a tentative note on vowel harmony, and word-final segments (overwhelmingly open syllables, possible -n). Chinese tone categories appear only incidentally (入声 codas as evidence for final stops). Nothing on accent, stress or tone of Paekche. text is machine scanned of fair quality; chapters 1-2 are the annotated toponym list.

sources.citation: Vovin, Alexander. 2013. From Koguryŏ to T'amna: Slowly riding to the South with speakers of Proto-Korean. Korean Linguistics 15(2): 222-240.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Re-examines Paekche/pseudo-Koguryŏ material; comparative, no prosody expected.

sources.citation: Lee, Ki-Moon & S. Robert Ramsey. 2011. A History of the Korean Language. Cambridge: CUP (ch. on Old Korean, Paekche section).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Standard handbook summary of what is and is not known about Paekche; would document the absence of phonological (let alone prosodic) reconstruction.

sources.citation: Vovin, Alexander. 2005. Koguryŏ and Paekche: Different Languages or Dialects of Old Korean? Journal of Inner and East Asian Studies 2(2): 108-140.

sources.note: Fullest modern philological treatment of the Paekche corpus; would confirm (almost certainly) that nothing prosodic is recoverable. Low expected yield.

sources.citation: Toh, Soo-hee. 1986. The Paekche Language: Its Formation and Features. Korean Linguistics 4: 33-46 (and his Korean-language 百濟語硏究 volumes, 1977-2000).

sources.note: The main Korean specialist on Paekche toponyms; only place a remark on prosody could conceivably appear, though the data cannot support one.

sources.note: Per the RISS record (title, keywords 'Old Korean; tone marks; Middle Chinese; Go-on; Kan-on') and as summarized in Park 2014/2015 (a work listed here, quoted there) and Park 2017 p. 49: Kwon compares the 聲點 on Korean-origin names in the Iwasaki-bon with Middle Chinese tone classes and with Go-on/Kan-on, finds MC 上/去 characters marked 平 (the '上·去 <-> a' correspondence), and argues this implies that the Old Korean tone system reflected in these names was quite different from the Middle Chinese system, i.e. that the marks reflect ancient Korean tone rather than Chinese tone.
